result.topic_en: Estimating the Dirichlet-type integral $\int_0^c \frac{\sin k\beta}{\sin\beta} f(\beta)\,d\beta$ by splitting it into an alternating sum of pieces between consecutive zeros and bounding it above and below to show it tends to $\frac{\pi}{2}f(0)$; a small separate slip has an algebraic calculation.
result.transcription:
$\int_0^c \frac{\sin k\beta}{\sin\beta} f(\beta)\,\partial\beta$ [figure] Im Fall daß die f einmal Maxima ergeben [?] und nicht [?] ... [?]
$= \frac{\pi}{2} f(0)$ Wir theilen das Integral in Integrale ein, während [?] deren f ... [?] ... [?]
$\int_0^c \frac{\sin k\beta}{\sin\beta} f(\beta)\partial\beta = \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{k}} + \int_{\frac{\pi}{k}}^{\frac{2\pi}{k}} + \cdots + \int_{\frac{m\pi}{k}} \cdots$
$J = r_1 - r_2 + r_3 - \cdots \pm r_{m+1}$ $r_\nu = \pm(-1)^{\nu-1}\int_{\frac{(\nu-1)\pi}{k}}^{\frac{\nu\pi}{k}} \frac{\sin k\beta}{\sin\beta} f(\beta)\partial\beta$
$r_\nu \leqq f\left(\frac{\nu-1\,\pi}{k}\right)\varrho_\nu$ $r_{\nu+1} \leqq f\left(\frac{\nu\pi}{k}\right)\varrho_{\nu+1}$
$\geqq f\left(\frac{\nu\pi}{k}\right)\varrho_\nu$ $r_1 \gtrless r_2 \gtrless r_3 \cdots \gtrless r_{m+1}$
$2\mu < m$
$J > r_1 - r_2 + \cdots - r_{2\mu}$ | $J < r_1 - r_2 + \cdots - r_{2\mu} + r_{2\mu+1}$
[-$J > \varrho_1 f\left(\frac{\pi}{k}\right) - \varrho_2 f\left(\frac{\pi}{k}\right) +$-] $J > \varrho_1 f\left(\frac{\pi}{k}\right) - \varrho_2 f\left(\frac{\pi}{k}\right) + \varrho_3 f\left(\frac{3\pi}{k}\right)$
$J < \varrho_1 f(0) - \varrho_2 f\frac{2\pi}{k} + \varrho_3$
$J > (\varrho_1 - \varrho_2) f\left(\frac{\pi}{k}\right) + (\varrho_3 - \varrho_4) f\left(\frac{3\pi}{k}\right)$ $J < \varrho_1 f(0) - f\left(\frac{2\pi}{k}\right)(\varrho_2 - \varrho_3) \cdots$
$+ (\varrho_{2\mu-1} - \varrho_{2\mu}) f\left(\frac{(2\mu-1)\pi}{k}\right)$ $J < \varrho_1 f(0) - f\frac{2\mu\pi}{k}(\varrho_2 - \varrho_3 \cdots$
$J \geqq (\varrho_1 - \varrho_2 + \varrho_3 \cdots - \varrho_{2\mu}) f\left(\frac{2\mu\pi}{k}\right)$ $+ \varrho_{2\mu+1})$
$\varrho_1 - \varrho_2 + \varrho_3 \cdots - \varrho_{2\mu} + \varrho_{2\mu+1} > \frac{\pi}{2}$ [-$\varrho_1 - \varrho_2 + \varrho_3 \cdots + \varrho_{2\mu} < \frac{\pi}{2}$-]
$J > \left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \varrho_{2\mu+1}\right) f\frac{2\mu\pi}{k}$ $J < \varrho_1 f(0) - \left(\varrho_1 - \frac{\pi}{2} - \varrho_{2\mu+1}\right)$
$J > \frac{\pi}{2} f\left(\frac{2\mu\pi}{k}\right) - \varrho_{2\mu+1} f\left(\frac{2\mu\pi}{k}\right)$ $J < \varrho_1 f(0) - \varrho_1 f\left(\frac{2\mu\pi}{k}\right) + \frac{\pi}{2} f\left(\frac{2\mu\pi}{k}\right)$
$+ \varrho_{2\mu+1} f\left(\frac{2\mu\pi}{k}\right)$

methods.what: Limit of the Dirichlet-type integral as k grows
Splitting the integral at the zeros $\nu\pi/k$ of $\sin k\beta$
Writing the integral as an alternating series of pieces
Bounding each piece by values of a monotone f times $\varrho_\nu$ (second mean-value-type estimate)
Upper and lower bounds from truncating the alternating sum

items.english: The alternating sum of the rho's up to $\varrho_{2\mu+1}$ exceeds $\pi/2$.
